3:1.sourceText: Κἀγώ, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἠδυνήθην λαλῆσαι ὑμῖν ὡς πνευματικοῖς ἀλλ’ ὡς σαρκίνοις, ὡς νηπίοις ἐν Χριστῷ.
3:1.targetText: And I, brothers, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly—as to babies in Christ;

3:2.sourceText: γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα, οὐ βρῶμα· οὔπω γὰρ ἐδύνασθε. Ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἔτι νῦν δύνασθε,
3:2.targetText: with milk I fed you, and not with meat, for you were not yet able, but not even yet are you now able,

groups.note: Actual ἐπότισα is the aorist give-to-drink verb with milk as its object, rendered I fed. Its original drinking/cause-to-drink head remains rather than a substituted Greek general feeding verb.
Actual βρῶμα is food, rendered meat in the older general food sense under the milk contrast. No separate Greek flesh/meat σάρξ noun is printed here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinates the milk and not-meat phrases with and. Pinned N1904 places the negated meat object directly after milk/you/I-fed without a separate conjunction.

3:3.sourceText: ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε. ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις, οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε;
3:3.targetText: for yet you are fleshly, for where [there is] among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are you not fleshly, and walk in the manner of men?

groups.note: Actual ἄνθρωπον is the singular man/human noun in the according-to-man idiom, rendered in the manner of men with its preposition. The English plural does not change the source singular form.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an existential copula in the where/envying-and-strife clause. Pinned N1904 has that location/conjunction and its noun subjects without a written be verb.
LSV adds the coordinated divisions noun. Pinned N1904 has envying and strife without that further conjunction/noun pair.

3:4.sourceText: ὅταν γὰρ λέγῃ τις Ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, ἕτερος δέ Ἐγὼ Ἀπολλῶ, οὐκ ἄνθρωποί ἐστε;
3:4.targetText: For when one may say, “I, indeed, am of Paul,” and another, “I—of Apollos,” are you not fleshly?

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἄνθρωποι is men/human beings. Pinned CrossWire TR instead prints σαρκικοί, matching LSV fleshly; the actual human noun and fleshly adjective remain distinct source-witness heads.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has fleshly, corroborated by the TR σαρκικοί adjective. Pinned N1904 instead has the actual men/human beings noun ἄνθρωποι; that different head is not relabeled as a fleshly adjective.

3:5.sourceText: τί οὖν ἐστιν Ἀπολλῶς; τί δέ ἐστιν Παῦλος; διάκονοι δι’ ὧν ἐπιστεύσατε, καὶ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Κύριος ἔδωκεν.
3:5.targetText: Who, then, is Paul, and who Apollos, but servants through whom you believed, and to each as the LORD gave?

groups.note: Greek writes is separately in both questions; English writes is once and leaves it understood in the coordinated second question. Both actual same-form predicates are retained in the one shared English selector.

The two name-bearing questions appear in opposite order: N1904 asks about Apollos then Paul; LSV names Paul then Apollos. Each actual name retains its own identity rather than being assigned by position.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 prints neuter τί, what, in its questions about Apollos and Paul. The pinned TR uses personal τίς, who, matching LSV’s who wording and reversed question order; the actual interrogative forms remain explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows the personal who question wording, corroborated by pinned TR τίς; pinned N1904 has neuter what for the question about these named workers.
LSV repeats the personal who question where pinned N1904 repeats neuter what; no different Greek pronoun form is invented.
The longer TR wording has an except/but transition before servants. Pinned N1904 proceeds directly to servants without a separate adversative particle at this position.

3:6.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἐφύτευσα, Ἀπολλῶς ἐπότισεν, ἀλλὰ ὁ Θεὸς ηὔξανεν·
3:6.targetText: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was giving growth;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

3:7.sourceText: ὥστε οὔτε ὁ φυτεύων ἐστίν τι οὔτε ὁ ποτίζων, ἀλλ’ ὁ αὐξάνων Θεός.
3:7.targetText: so that neither is he who is planting anything, nor he who is watering, but He who is giving growth—God;

3:8.sourceText: ὁ φυτεύων δὲ καὶ ὁ ποτίζων ἕν εἰσιν, ἕκαστος δὲ τὸν ἴδιον μισθὸν λήμψεται κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον κόπον.
3:8.targetText: and he who is planting and he who is watering are one, and each will receive his own reward according to his own labor,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with the two his-own phrases.

3:9.sourceText: Θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί· Θεοῦ γεώργιον, Θεοῦ οἰκοδομή ἐστε.
3:9.targetText: for we are fellow-workmen of God; you are God’s tillage, God’s building.

3:10.sourceText: Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὡς σοφὸς ἀρχιτέκτων θεμέλιον ἔθηκα, ἄλλος δὲ ἐποικοδομεῖ. ἕκαστος δὲ βλεπέτω πῶς ἐποικοδομεῖ.
3:10.targetText: According to the grace of God that was given to me, as a wise master-builder, I have laid a foundation, and another builds on [it],

groups.note: The actual foundation laid is the same immediate base of the coordinated other-builder predicate. English resumes that written foundation as [it]; both mentions retain the one actual foundation noun, without a separately printed Greek object pronoun.
Actual ἔθηκα is aorist indicative, rendered I have laid. Its source remains the aorist placing form rather than a Greek perfect.

unmappedSource.reason: Pinned N1904 ends this verse with each / and / let-see / how / builds-on. That final caution clause is absent both from installed LSV and from its pinned76-1COenglsv.usfm3:10 source; no English counterpart is fabricated for those actual Greek words.

3:11.sourceText: θεμέλιον γὰρ ἄλλον οὐδεὶς δύναται θεῖναι παρὰ τὸν κείμενον, ὅς ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός.
3:11.targetText: for no one is able to lay another foundation except that which is laid, which is Jesus the Christ;

groups.note: Actual κείμενον is the lying/being-laid participle used of the foundation, rendered is laid. The source remains κεῖμαι rather than an independently written τίθημι passive form.

3:12.sourceText: εἰ δέ τις ἐποικοδομεῖ ἐπὶ τὸν θεμέλιον χρυσίον, ἀργύριον, λίθους τιμίους, ξύλα, χόρτον, καλάμην,
3:12.targetText: and if anyone builds on this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw—

groups.note: The actual build-on compound and following explicit ἐπί preposition share the one English builds-on construction; both written source constituents remain in this group rather than duplicating the English on word.

unmappedSource.reason: The source article identifies the foundation; English uses a demonstrative determiner instead of a separate definite article.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly says this foundation. Pinned N1904 has the definite foundation without an independently written demonstrative here.

3:13.sourceText: ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον φανερὸν γενήσεται· ἡ γὰρ ἡμέρα δηλώσει, ὅτι ἐν πυρὶ ἀποκαλύπτεται, καὶ ἑκάστου τὸ ἔργον ὁποῖόν ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ αὐτὸ δοκιμάσει.
3:13.targetText: the work will become visible of each, for the day will declare [it], because it is revealed in fire, and the work of each, what kind it is, the fire will prove;

groups.note: The actual work is the subject of becoming visible and the same immediately declared object under the causal day clause. English repeats [it] for that one work; no separate Greek object pronoun with declare is printed.

Actual ἐστιν is the third-person singular finite be verb in the what-kind clause. English it is states that predicate with its required English subject; no separate Greek subject pronoun is printed inside this clause.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual αὐτό has P-NSN (nominative singular neuter) in both pinned functional and form analyses. The written form can also be accusative, but that ambiguity does not establish an accusative work-object role or a link to the English subject inside what-kind-it-is. LSV does not separately express this token; the pinned CrossWire TR sequence omits αὐτό here. The actual N1904 form and nominative analysis are retained without a guessed target. Form paradigm: https://doxa.billmounce.com/BBG4_Workbook_Key.pdf . Primary comparative apparatus: https://github.com/Faithlife/SBLGNT/blob/master/data/sblgntapp/xml/1Cor.xml .

3:14.sourceText: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον μενεῖ ὃ ἐποικοδόμησεν, μισθὸν λήμψεται·
3:14.targetText: if the work of anyone remains that he built on [it], he will receive a wage;

groups.note: Actual μενεῖ is future indicative will remain, rendered present remains within the conditional clause. Its source future form is retained.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the base object after built on. The actual relative ὃ refers to the work built, not a separately written foundation/base pronoun after the build-on predicate.

3:15.sourceText: εἴ τινος τὸ ἔργον κατακαήσεται, ζημιωθήσεται, αὐτὸς δὲ σωθήσεται, οὕτως δὲ ὡς διὰ πυρός.
3:15.targetText: if the work of any is burned up, he will suffer loss, but himself will be saved, but so as through fire.

groups.note: Actual κατακαήσεται is future passive, rendered is burned up within the condition; the source future is retained rather than changed to Greek present.

3:16.sourceText: Οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ναὸς Θεοῦ ἐστε καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν οἰκεῖ;
3:16.targetText: Have you not known that you are a temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?

3:17.sourceText: εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός· ὁ γὰρ ναὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἅγιός ἐστιν, οἵτινές ἐστε ὑμεῖς.
3:17.targetText: If anyone ruins the temple of God, God will ruin him; for the temple of God is holy, which you are.

groups.note: Actual οἵτινες is the masculine plural relative referring to the addressed people, whom English relates back to the temple designation with which. The original plural personal relative remains rather than a changed singular/neuter form.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with God.

3:18.sourceText: Μηδεὶς ἑαυτὸν ἐξαπατάτω· εἴ τις δοκεῖ σοφὸς εἶναι ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ, μωρὸς γενέσθω, ἵνα γένηται σοφός,
3:18.targetText: Let no one deceive himself; if anyone seems to be wise among you in this age—let him become a fool, that he may become wise,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with the demonstrative this age.

3:19.sourceText: ἡ γὰρ σοφία τοῦ κόσμου τούτου μωρία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἐστιν. γέγραπται γάρ Ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν·
3:19.targetText: for the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God, for it has been written: “Who is taking the wise in their craftiness”;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with God or their craftiness.

3:20.sourceText: καὶ πάλιν Κύριος γινώσκει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς τῶν σοφῶν, ὅτι εἰσὶν μάταιοι.
3:20.targetText: and again, “The LORD knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are vain.”

3:21.sourceText: ὥστε μηδεὶς καυχάσθω ἐν ἀνθρώποις· πάντα γὰρ ὑμῶν ἐστιν,
3:21.targetText: So then, let no one glory in men, for all things are yours,

3:22.sourceText: εἴτε Παῦλος εἴτε Ἀπολλῶς εἴτε Κηφᾶς, εἴτε κόσμος εἴτε ζωὴ εἴτε θάνατος, εἴτε ἐνεστῶτα εἴτε μέλλοντα, πάντα ὑμῶν,
3:22.targetText: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things about to be—all are yours,

groups.note: Actual ἐνεστῶτα is the perfect present/being-at-hand participle used substantivally, rendered things present; no independently printed things noun is claimed.
Actual μέλλοντα is the present participle of the impending/be-about-to verb, used substantivally, rendered things about to be; no independent Greek be infinitive or things noun is printed here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula in this repeated all/yours statement. Pinned N1904 lists the alternatives and concludes all/yours without an independently written be verb in this verse.

3:23.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ Χριστοῦ, Χριστὸς δὲ Θεοῦ.
3:23.targetText: and you [are] Christ’s, and Christ [is] God’s.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula with you/Christ’s; pinned N1904 has the personal subject and genitive possessor without a written be verb in this verse.
English supplies the copula with Christ/God’s; pinned N1904 has that subject and genitive possessor without a written be verb here.
